title: Re-running the safetywashing capability-correlation test on 2025-era governance benchmarks

original_idea.body:
# Re-running the safetywashing capability-correlation test on 2025-era governance benchmarks

**Problem:** Ren et al. (2024) showed many safety benchmarks correlate strongly with raw capabilities ('safetywashing'). Newer governance-relevant evals (refusal, jailbreak-robustness, agentic-misuse benchmarks released in 2025) were not in that study.

**Direction:** Follow up by applying the published safetywashing methodology (their open GitHub code computes capability-correlation) to a fresh set of 2025 safety/governance benchmarks using public leaderboard scores across open models. Report which new benchmarks are capability-entangled and which measure something orthogonal, extending their analysis.

**Why it matters:** Regulators increasingly cite benchmark scores as evidence of safety; knowing which 2025 benchmarks are confounded by capability prevents policy from rewarding mere scaling. Uses public scores and existing open-source code, no training.

**Relevant context:** Ren et al. 2024 'Safetywashing' (NeurIPS, open code at centerforaisafety/safetywashing); Generation Strategy Hint FR67 (vary AI Safety Index / benchmark methodology).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying capability-confounded safety benchmarks directly prevents policy rewarding scaling as safety, a strong explicit chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reuses published open code on public leaderboard scores; clear inherited methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused extension with defined benchmarks and metric, some data-collection effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Third-party benchmark scrutiny on public data; labs disincentivized.

low_compute.reasoning: Uses public scores and analysis code, no training.

novelty.reasoning: Direct methodological replication on newer benchmarks; angle plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Extending safetywashing to 2025 benchmarks is a fresh slice likely untested.
